trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
I can't rule out up, down or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Cell (2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,5). So the line goes right.
Going up, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5). So the line goes right.
Going up would leave both cell (1,4) and cell (1,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
The line must go up: down is number 11, which comes later.
Going down would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
